newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle quiet, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle quiet, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets remained quiet Thursday, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
Market sources earlier in the week had anticipated that packers would buy cattle steady with last week's top price of $72.00 per cwt, but they never wavered from bids at $70.00.
Cattle owners also held firm at their asking level of $72.00 confident that packers were running short on supply and would need to start buying cattle soon.
Neither side budged, resulting in the stalemate and talk that packers would be in the market Friday.
Some of the packer reluctance to pay $72.00 was attributed to slipping boxed beef prices which eroded packer operating margins, market sources said.
Boxed beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.11 to $0.69, with 166 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
Choice heavyweight boxed beef prices have declined $1.03 since Tuesday's close.
